literal.prompt: Какой климатический режим характеризуется противоположными аномалиями температуры поверхности моря в западной и восточной частях тропического бассейна, которым сопутствуют противоположные изменения осадков?

sourceReasons: CPC IOD specifically defines opposite western/eastern equatorial INDIAN Ocean SST departures and the associated East African/Maritime Continent rainfall contrast. This confirms answer 2 as an intended answer, not unique identification by the current basin-free wording.

NWS ENSO defines El Niño as warmer central/eastern tropical Pacific SST with rainfall decreasing over Indonesia and increasing farther east. Its definition does not state that the western tropical Pacific SST has no opposite-sign anomaly. The new generic question does not name the Indian basin or distinguish the African/Indonesian pair from this Pacific climate mode.

NWS ENSO defines La Niña as cooler central/eastern Pacific SST with rainfall increasing over Indonesia and decreasing farther east. This is also a tropical SST/rainfall contrast; the saved definitions do not establish the exclusion of this alternative under the current unrestricted west/east wording.
CPC IOD confirms the exact SST dipole but locates it specifically in the Indian Ocean. The identifying geographical scope has been removed from CURRENT.
CPC NAO defines an atmospheric height/pressure dipole over Greenland and central North Atlantic. It is distinguishable from an ocean SST tropical dipole, so answer 3 is a sound distractor.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: The direct ocean-name/key matching defect is removed. However, «тропического бассейна» now leaves the basin unidentified. Opposed west/east SST and rainfall is not shown here to uniquely exclude ENSO phases. Do not accept intended-key support as proof of a unique key; this unresolved discrimination issue is HOLD after the single fix-cycle.

fieldGroups.literal: Диполь Индийского океана (IOD) — режим межгодовой изменчивости температуры поверхности моря в тропическом бассейне. При смене фазы тёплая и холодная аномалии меняются местами, а осадки в Восточной Африке и районе Индонезии обычно реагируют противоположно.
sourceReasons: CPC calls IOD an intrinsic climate-variability mode, describes positive western warmth/eastern cooling and their reversal in the negative phase. Its rainfall paragraph gives opposite East African and Maritime Continent responses in the two phases; Indonesia is within the Maritime Continent. Interannual variability describes the climate mode rather than a daily weather event.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Two clear sentences identify the mode and phase behavior without turning a tendency into an absolute rule.

fieldGroups.literal: Эль-Ниньо — фаза ЭНЮК с аномально тёплой поверхностью центральной и восточной тропической части Тихого океана.
sourceReasons: NWS ENSO El Niño paragraph directly gives warming of the central and eastern tropical Pacific surface. Opening ENSO definition and the three phase descriptions establish it as an ENSO phase.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Independent term definition, not a negative placeholder; below 35 words.

fieldGroups.literal: При Ла-Нинье поверхность центральной и восточной тропической части Тихого океана холоднее среднего, а обычные восточные ветры усиливаются.
sourceReasons: NWS ENSO La Niña paragraph explicitly gives below-average SST in the central/eastern tropical Pacific and strengthening of the normal easterly winds.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Independent phase fact, correct declension «при Ла-Нинье», below 35 words.

fieldGroups.literal: Его индекс — разность аномалий температуры поверхности моря на западе и востоке экваториального Индийского океана; положительная фаза обычно усиливает дожди в Восточной Африке.
sourceReasons: CPC IOD paragraph 3 defines DMI as western-minus-eastern equatorial Indian SST departures from average; paragraph 4 says positive IOD tends to increase rainfall in equatorial East Africa. The rainfall tendency is an additional fact beyond the asked identification/contrast.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Adds DMI definition and East African rainfall tendency; meets the correct-note additional-fact requirement.

fieldGroups.literal: Североатлантическое колебание — диполь атмосферных аномалий между районом Гренландии и центральной частью Северной Атлантики.
sourceReasons: CPC NAO definition places the anomaly centers over Greenland and the central North Atlantic (35–40°N), with opposite sign. Atmospheric anomalies are faithful to height/pressure anomalies in that definition.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Independent location/structure fact for NAO, below 35 words.

neighborReview.reason: Pacific/Indonesia rainfall shift identifies El Niño; IOD asks an Indian-basin SST dipole, so the facts are distinct. New IOD wording no longer identifies the Indian basin: no exact keyed fact duplicate is established, but answer discriminability against these ENSO phases remains unresolved.

La Niña card asks stronger equatorial easterlies, distinct from Indian SST east–west contrast. New IOD wording no longer identifies the Indian basin: no exact keyed fact duplicate is established, but answer discriminability against these ENSO phases remains unresolved.
NAO card asks an atmospheric north–south pressure/height dipole; IOD is an ocean SST east–west mode.
Monsoon card asks seasonal moist airflow to the Indian subcontinent, not interannual opposed SST anomalies.

defects.description: CURRENT omits which tropical basin or which regions define the SST dipole. CPC supports an Indian-basin mode, while the offered ENSO phases also involve tropical ocean SST and opposed Indonesia/Pacific rainfall changes. Available saved text does not prove their exclusion under the generic wording. This is an editorial/uniqueness HOLD, not a claim that CPC fails to support IOD.

literal.prompt: Какой климат отличается сухим летом и мягкой влажной зимой?

sourceReasons: Met Office Mediterranean section directly identifies this climate by dry summers and mild wet winters; index 1 is unique among the offered climate types.
Met Office tropical rainforest section describes high temperatures and year-round rain near the equator, not Mediterranean seasonality.
Met Office Mediterranean section defines dry summers and mild wet winters.
Met Office Desert section describes extreme dryness and thermal swings, rather than a distinct mild wet winter.
Met Office Polar section defines prolonged cold and no monthly mean over 10 °C, unlike the mild Mediterranean winter.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: All four consistent nominative noun phrases answer «Какой климат ...?». Climate types form a coherent category. Dry versus year-round wet or prolonged cold distinctions are broadly known school geography and appropriate for easy; no name-matching key leak.

fieldGroups.literal: Средиземноморский климат — разновидность умеренного: лето в нём сухое, а зима мягкая и влажная. Он встречается на западных окраинах материков, в том числе за пределами Средиземноморского бассейна.
sourceReasons: Met Office Mediterranean section explicitly calls it a specific type of temperate climate, gives dry summers/mild wet winters, and states occurrence on western coasts of continents and outside the Mediterranean Basin.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Two sentences give the key, classification and geographic distribution; under 70 words.

fieldGroups.literal: У экватора солнечные лучи падают почти отвесно и дают сильный прогрев поверхности; в полярных широтах они идут под гораздо меньшим углом.
sourceReasons: NWS Flight Environment opening Hemispheric Prevailing Winds paragraphs explicitly attribute maximum solar heating near the equator to more direct rays and much weaker polar heating to oblique rays. This is a relevant physical fact about the equatorial climate option.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Independent solar-incidence fact connects specifically to the equatorial option; grammar and length acceptable.

fieldGroups.literal: Он встречается также в Калифорнии, Западной Австралии, Чили и Южной Африке; характерная растительность включает chaparral и fynbos.
sourceReasons: Met Office Mediterranean section lists California, parts of Western Australia, Chile and South Africa, and names chaparral and fynbos vegetation. These are useful facts additional to the asked seasons. Latin-script names are understandable scientific names, though Russian transliteration would read more naturally; that is advisory only.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Useful geographic and vegetation facts go beyond the seasonal key, under 35 words. Transliteration of botanical names is optional polish, not an acceptance blocker.

fieldGroups.literal: Пустыни крайне засушливы; ясное небо способствует большим перепадам температуры, а ночью там может быть ниже нуля.
sourceReasons: Met Office Desert section explicitly gives extreme dryness, large swings due to cloudless skies, and nights below freezing in many deserts. The note says temperatures can drop below zero, not that every desert necessarily does.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Independent dryness/temperature fact specific to the desert option; grammatically complete and under 35 words.

fieldGroups.literal: В полярном климате средняя температура ни одного месяца не превышает 10 °C; в климате ледникового покрова среднемесячная температура ни одного месяца не превышает 0 °C.
sourceReasons: Met Office Polar climate section specifies no month with mean temperature above 10 °C and specifically ice cap climate with no month averaging above 0 °C. CURRENT now explicitly says «в климате ледникового покрова» and «среднемесячная температура», faithfully restricting the second threshold to that subtype.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: The terrain-versus-climate scope defect is resolved. Complete standalone note, correct agreement and temperature means; under 35 words.
